text:
alex: Heads-up — noticed a jump in token-level validation time on /generate-tool at ~03:10 UTC. Heatmap shows latency buckets shifting right, and the token breakdown panel spikes on the validation stage. anyone on this?
maria: yep saw that on the per-route KPIs. median validation_time went from ~12ms -> ~45ms, p95 ~180ms. retries for tool calls increased ~2x around the same time.
devon: I pulled a short flamegraph from the profiler for a sample request. ~40% of CPU time in structured schema validation (jsonschema.validate), ~15% in kernel selection path (kernel_chooser) thanks to repeated kernel warmups.
alex: kernel selector? we rolled kernel-selection heuristic last night to prefer mixed-precision fallback for some model variants. could be related. also curious about kv-cache churn.
pat: noticed KV prefetch churn in the same window — eviction rate spiked, and the kv-hit ratio dropped. that leads to more cache misses and extra KV rehydration which increases kernel churn.
deploy-bot: deploy-bot: canary rollout 2026-03-15T03:07 UTC — runtime: kernel-selector v2.3, batching-heuristic v1.9.2, tool-validate-service v3.0.
maria: timeline aligns with that canary. regression looks like an interaction: new kernel selector + prefetch/backpressure -> more kernel swaps -> longer validation because validation runs while kvcache is cold.
devon: reproduced locally with a curl loop. Short reproducer attached in gist (private). Microbench results: full jsonschema validation costs ~= 6-12ms per token for large structured outputs; when retries happen it multiplies. Quick experiment: added a "shallow schema" fast-pass that checks types and required fields then defers heavy checks — cut validation tail latency by ~60%.
alex: proposed mitigation plan:
- change kernel selector to prefer previously-used kernels for seq_len <= 128 to avoid fp32 fallbacks on warmup
- add shallow validation pass (cheap) before full jsonschema, with metric tag `validation_stage` to split cheap/expensive times
- add prefetch backoff to reduce eviction storms under bursty traffic
- add new per-route alert: validation_time.p95 > 100ms
pat: I'll open a tiny PR for shallow validation + metrics. will add an opt-in flag on the route so we can toggle quickly.
maria: please also add a dashboard row showing validation_time split by `validation_stage` and by route. and a token-level stacked bar for kernel_warmup vs kv_miss vs validation.
devon: sending `perf.tar.gz` with flamegraph and a small `curl` reproducer to the thread (uploaded to infra S3). Also adding a script to run microbench with/without shallow pass.
alex: nice. after PR/metrics we can roll to a canary subset (same as deploy-bot canary) and watch the heatmap for bucket movement. if we see improvement we'll roll.
pat: PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/482 — includes `validation_stage` metric and shallow-pass implementation.
maria: added alert on staging: `validation_time.p95 > 100ms` for /generate-tool and /structured-output routes.
devon: experiment numbers look good. shallow-pass -> p95 down from 180ms -> ~70ms in microbench; kernel-selector tweak on the canary nodes drops kernel warmup events by ~40%.
alex: sound plan. let's coordinate a targeted canary tonight. thanks all :thumbsup:
